title: Tenet
one_line: A spy film cut as a palindrome: the second half runs back through the first, and the only day the film names is the day it both starts and ends.

anchor.label: the 14th
anchor.note: The one day the film names. The Kyiv opera siege, Sator's planned death on the yacht in Vietnam, and the Stalsk-12 detonation all fall on it. No month or year is shown.

durations_stated.what: Kat needs days inverted for the wound to heal
The Oslo freeport turnstile is about a week before Tallinn

colour_code.note: The Stalsk-12 assault names its forward team red and its inverted team blue, each with ten minutes. The same two colours mark the two sides of every turnstile room. On this page, red is anything moving forward in time and blue is anything inverted.

rules.rule: Inversion is done with a turnstile. You walk in moving forward and walk out moving backward, and you meet yourself on the way.
An inverted bullet un-fires: it leaves the wall and returns to the gun. Barbara shows the Protagonist one in the briefing.
Inverted people cannot breathe ordinary air. They carry their own.
Fire runs the wrong way for an inverted body. An explosion freezes you rather than burning you.
The film's own line for free will inside a fixed sequence is "What's happened, happened". Neil adds that it is faith in the mechanics of the world, not an excuse to do nothing.
The grandfather paradox is raised and left open: the future may be gambling that it does not apply.

sator_square.note: A Latin word square that reads the same forwards, backwards, up and down. The film's five proper nouns are its five words, and TENET sits across the middle both ways.

modes.label: World clock
modes.note: The same events in the order they happen, with the 14th first.
